rules_applied.protocol_holdout_sealing: No predictor is fitted, scored or tuned on any block-5 outcome before the look. Every read of a block-5 outcome by the harness is logged to the holdout access log.
rules_applied.protocol_holdout_a_technical_rerun: If the look fails for a technical reason, the fix must not depend on any holdout result. Each rerun is a further logged access, and the report states the number of accesses.

disclosed_before_the_look.text: Verification after the look replays the look through Harness.look against temporary logs; it never touches the real access log, and no test or script reads a block-5 outcome any other way.
disclosed_before_the_look.note: The replay design was disclosed before the look: temporary logs, the real access log untouched. It did not say the replays would be counted and it did not reconcile with the protocol's counting rule; the owner's decision does.

A run made on purpose is still two counted accesses (a CI run with the switch set would be two for each job of the matrix) and is added to this record when it is made.

replay_tests_policy.what_it_changes: the default suite shows the nine replay tests as skipped, in addition to the tests that were already skipped, and a push no longer adds counted accesses
replay_tests_policy.what_it_does_not_change: the count so far, the chained access log, the decision to count replays as accesses, or what the replay tests check when they are run; the replay tests were not run again when they were made opt-in, so the count is unchanged

The totals were 17 when the decision was made and 21 in all; they are 19 and 25.
corrections.how_found: the owner asked for a check of the CI run of the opt-in push; its jobs list showed two jobs, and the jobs of runs #232 and #233 showed both had run the test step to success

what_the_replays_did: Each replay re-ran the look's pipeline on the same 23 events and compared its outputs with the committed ones; the runs passed, or (R2 to R5) failed exactly the tests that should notice the deliberate alteration. Nothing was selected, tuned, changed or decided from them, and no result was read from them that the committed outputs do not already hold.

limits: The count is a lower bound: it rests on the session transcript and the CI API. A run by someone else, or a run not visible to either, is not in it.

The replays' own access records were written to temporary logs that were deleted; nothing in them survives, so the count cannot be checked against them.
These accesses are not in the hash-chained access log, which is written before an outcome is read by a run against the real log. The chained log is unchanged.
R9 and R10 were counted in advance in the first version of this record and are recorded here as they happened, from the transcript and the CI API.
